1.q: כִּ֠י בְּ⁠לֵ֞יל שֻׁדַּ֨ד עָ֤ר מוֹאָב֙ נִדְמָ֔ה כִּ֗י בְּ⁠לֵ֛יל שֻׁדַּ֥ד קִיר־מוֹאָ֖ב נִדְמָֽה׃
1.note: The expressions **is devastated** and **is destroyed** are in a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is enemies. Alternate translation: [For in the night when enemies devastated it, and they destroyed Ar of Moab. For in the night when enemies devastated it, and they destroyed Kir of Moab]

2.note: Isaiah is speaking of **Moab** as if it were a living thing that could wail. He means that the people of the nation of Moab wail. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The people of Moab wail over harm done to the towns of Nebo and Medeba]

Shaving the head and cutting off the beard were symbolic actions by which people showed that they were mourning. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [All of its people shave their heads and cut off their beards to show that they are mourning]

Isaiah says **all of its heads** as a generalization for emphasis. He means that very many of the Moabite men shaved their heads. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [very many of its heads]

The expression **is cut off** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is the Moabites themselves. Alternate translation: [each man has cut off his beard]

3.note: Wearing sackcloth was a symbolic action by which people showed that they were mourning. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [they put on sackcloth to show that they are mourning]
The pronoun **they** refers to the people of Moab in general. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the people of Moab gird on sackcloth]

Isaiah is referring to all the places where the Moabites will be mourning by naming two major components, **its housetops** and **its squares**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Everywhere in the city]

Isaiah says **all of it wails** as a generalization for emphasis. He means that very many of the people of Moab wail. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [everyone wails]

4.note: Isaiah is speaking of the cities **Heshbon** and **Elealeh** as if they were living things that could cry out. He means that the people of those cities cry out. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And the people of Heshbon and Elealeh cry out]

The expression **is heard** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [their voice reaches]

Isaiah is using the adjective **armed** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [the soldiers of Moab]

The pronouns **his** and **him** refer to a representative **armed** soldier of **Moab**. It may be more natural in your language to use plural forms here. Alternate translation: [their souls tremble within them]

Here, the **soul** represents the whole person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [he trembles inside] or [they tremble inside]

5.note: Here Isaiah is speaking as if his emotions were his **heart** that could cry out. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I grieve deeply for Moab]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **destruction**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [an outcry because they are being destroyed]

6.note: Here Isaiah is speaking as if the waters of Nimrim were **desolations**, meaning dry wastelands. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the waters of Nimrim have become dry wastelands]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **desolations**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [completely dried up]

7.note: The terms **the abundance one has made** and **their store** mean similar things. Isaiah is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [the things they have accumulated and saved]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **abundance**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the plentiful goods]

8.note: Isaiah is speaking of **the outcry** as if it were a living thing that could travel around the border. He means that people are crying out throughout the territory of Moab. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The people are crying out everywhere within Moab]

9.note: Here, **blood** represents the death and violence that has taken place. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [flow with the blood of those who have been killed]

Here Isaiah is speaking on behalf of Yahweh, and so he uses the pronoun **I**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this as Isaiah speaking about Yahweh, and you could use Yahweh’s name instead of that pronoun. The UST models one way to do this. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will put additions]

Yahweh is referring to all the surviving Moabites by naming two major components, **the escape of Moab** and **the remnant of the land**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [destruction for those who flee from Moab and destruction for those who remain in the land]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the coming judgment were **a lion** that would attack the Moabites. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [destruction for those who would escape from Moab]
